epigrafe.descrizione: A silver Roman finger ring, Henig Type XI, dating to the 2nd - 3rd century AD. The ring has a flat rectangular bezel with tapering shoulders and narrowed hoop. The bezel is decorated with two bands of inscised hatching above and below, each band being separated by an incised transverse line. A short vertically incised line defines the rectangle to the right and to the left. Within the rectangle…

epigrafe.descrizione: CURATOR'S REPORT. Description of find. Roman coin; struck gold aureus of Carausius (286-293). Found in association with DENO-64DAE1. Gold Aureus (20mm; 4.65g; Die Axis 12) London. Obverse: Helmeted and cuirassed bust of emperor facing left, looking glum. VIRTVS CAR/AVSI. Rev. Draped figure of Pax facing left, holding branch in front of her and sceptre behind. PAX AVG No mint mark. The coins. Both the coins were struck in the reign of Carausius (AD 286-93), one at the mint of London, the other the mint of Rouen. Gold coins of Carausius are extremely rare, these two specimens increasing the corpus of Huvelin from 23 to 25 - 15 for London and 10 for Rouen. (4 of the coins in Huvelin's corpus…

Depicts Livia, as Pax, holding long sceptre and olive branch, seated right on throne with ornate legs, single line below. Minted in Lugdunum. RIC 30. A similar example is featured in Moorhead, S. (2013, p. 57.). Dimensions. Weight: 2.67g. Diameter: 17mm. Reference: Moorhead, S. 2013. A History of Roman Coinage in Britain. Witham: Greenlight pub

Reverse: Wreath around VOT/X. Inscription: CAESARVM N(O STRORVM). Reece period 16. Mint: London. Mint mark: -//PLONU. Die axis: 6 o'clock. The coin is struck a little off centre, some wear, green patina with an area of green verdigris. This coin dates to 323-324AD. Ref. RIC VII, P.115, 292. The coin is 19.10mm long, 18.25mm wide, 1.79mm thick, diameter 19.10mm and weighs 2.3g

Inscription: Illegible. Reverse: Standing figure probably Salus at an altar, feeding a snake with 'S(C)' in the field. Inscription: SA(LVS AVG). Mint name: Rome. Die axis: 300 deg. or 10 o'clock. Worn and very corroded especially the obverse. However, there are some traces of intact green patina on the reverse and a few of the letters are legible. Ref. Coins of England and the UK, Spink 2009, page 52

epigrafe.provenienza: contea di ritrovamento: Lincolnshire (Inghilterra e Galles)
epigrafe.descrizione: An incomplete Roman silver 'ToT' ring of Henig type VIII. The ring has a circular bezel and incomplete triangular shoulders. The shoulders are worn but each one is decorated with two pellets, one in each surviving corner. The bezel is inscribed with two serrifed 'T's with a pellet between. The inscription T.T is an abbreviation of the Celtic god-name Totatis. Rings bearing the inscription ToT are commonly found in the East Midlands, especially in Lincolnshire

The bezel is worn but decorated with an incised border. A feint letter 'o' is visible in the centre, presumably the central letter of the inscription TOT for the god name Totatis. epigrafe.provenienza: contea di ritrovamento: Norfolk (Inghilterra e Galles)
epigrafe.descrizione: Fragment of Samien ware dating to the Roman period (45-410AD). The fragment is from the centre of the base of a vessel. It is circular in plan and D-shaped in profile. The fabric is very hard is light orange in colour and has an orange/red 'satin' gloss slip on both the inner and outer surface. The base is stamped with the inscription CATVSSAM, which is the stamp of the potter CATVSSA. The fragment was produced at Lezoux between 125-140. . In “Roman Samian Pottery in Britain”, Paul Webster (1996) notes that red-slip coated samian ware, made mainly in Gaul and Germany, was imported into Britain from the mid 1st to the mid 3rd centuries

epigrafe.provenienza: contea di ritrovamento: North Lincolnshire (Inghilterra e Galles)
epigrafe.descrizione: Gold coin. Merovingian ‘national series’ tremissis of Metz mint, as kindly identified by the finder, pierced with a probably drilled hole of diameter 1.6mm at 3 O’clock obverse. Suggested date: Early Medieval, 587-670. Obverse description: Bust diademed and cuirassed right. Obverse inscription: METTIS CIVETATI *. Reverse description: plain cross in wreath; V C[reversed] in upper angles; plain initial cross. Reverse inscription: +ANSOALDVS M[O]NET, piercing through O. Diameter: 14.4mm, Weight: 1.23gms, die axis: 12. The piercing of the coin may be intended to convert it to an amulet with the cross displayed, perhaps as a miniature and ready-made version of the pendants…

epigrafe.descrizione: A Roman gold finger-ring with solid stepped rectangular bezel. The hoop, distorted and incomplete, comprises an oval-sectioned, ribbed rod, smooth on the outer face. At the shoulders it is fused to the base of the bezel and enclosed by three pellets. The bezel has a short two-line inscription incised on its lightly-cambered surface. Wear, also apparent on the hoop and shoulders, has partially erased the inscription, which appears to read _ IV / _ II, perhaps [V]IV(AS) (ie. 'Long life to you .....') followed by an abbreviated personal name. The ring form is paralleled by an example from Baden im Aargau (F. epigrafe.descrizione: Fragment of Early Roman copper alloy possibly Hod Hill Aucissa derivative brooch. The bow is intact but the catchplate and hinge pin are missing. The hinge for the pin was formed by the rolling of the head back onto itself with a verticle slot for the pin. There is some moulded decoration across the breadth of the head and possibly a stamp or inscription. The bow has a central ridge decorated with 2 bands down its length. The bow curves out in a similar manner to an aucissa brooch. There is a small knop to either side at the top of the bow. The fragment is 30mm long, 15mm wide, 8mm thick and weighs 3.23g. This type of brooch dates from c. 43-70 AD. This brooch is similar to examples in…

epigrafe.provenienza: contea di ritrovamento: North Yorkshire (Inghilterra e Galles)
epigrafe.descrizione: A complete but broken finger ring of Roman date. The finger ring has a flat rectangular cross section with an expanded ovate bezel. The bezel has a deep groove running horizontally separating an inscription in two lines, one above the other below the line. The inscription is very shallow and worn though the upper text appears to read AVI and the lower VILA or VICA. The metal has a mid green patina and is worn. The finger ring is 20.7mm long, 8.5mm wide, 1mm thick and weighs 1.8g
epigrafe.licenza_metadati: CC BY-SA 4.0 (schede del PAS su Wikimedia Commons)

epigrafe.descrizione: Three decorated sherds of Samian type Roman pottery probably dating to the 2nd century AD (120 - 220 AD). All three sherds are made of the same fabric; however the decoration on each is different suggesting that they are from three different vessels. The fabric of each is a hard and fine grained with mica limestone and black iron ore inclusions. The fabric is assessed by observation of worn rather than fresh breaks. The slip / glaze on all three sherds is similar being relatively thick and a mid brown red colour. Where the sherds have been abraded the slip has been removed to reveal the buff orange brown coloured fabric beneath. This type of fabric and glaze is best compared to that of…

epigrafe.descrizione: A Roman silver denarius of Hadrian (AD 117-138) dating from AD 119-121. Mint of Rome. RIC II, p.352, no.101. Dimensions: diameter: 18.88mm; weight: 3.04g. Obverse description: Laureate bust right. Obverse inscription: IMP CAESAR TRAIAN HADRIANVS AVG. Reverse description: Victory advancing right holding trophy with both hands. Reverse inscription: P M TR P COS III
epigrafe.fotografo: The Portable Antiquities Scheme, Stuart Wyatt
